comment: Declares every vendor plugin row this repo disables and replaces, and what the
replacement owes it. Read by scripts/check-replacement-parity.mjs; the rule it
enforces is CONSTITUTION.md's 'A replacement never subtracts'.
`forks[].sha256` is the first 16 hex of the sha256 of the vendor file AS OF the
commit named by `vendorPin` — the revision each fork was last read against, not
a checksum of the fork itself. When a pin bump changes one of those files, the
check goes red until a human re-reads it beside the fork, ports what changed,
and re-records the hash with `--update`.
`divergences` records the places a replacement deliberately does NOT match the
row it replaces. Nothing enforces these; they exist so the next pin bump can
tell an intended difference from an omission.
`forkOnly` is for a package that forks a vendor FILE without disabling any
vendor plugin row, so checks 1-4 have nothing to judge. Only the fork-hash
check (5) runs over these, which is the one that forces the by-hand re-read
a pin bump needs.
`retirements` is for a vendor row this repo switches off and inserts NO
replacement for, because the capability it carried already lives on a surface
this repo owns. There is no replacement package to compare against, so check
6 asks the questions that still have answers: is the disable real, does the
row still exist upstream, what covers it now, and what was actually given up.
`divergences` may not be empty — a disabled row always costs something.

adds: renders the optional workspaceFilesNode service's Component as a Files sibling row
ORs the per-session everOpenedFile bit into all three pristine blank-phase gates
divergences: Entering a conversation activates the landing View (Chat) instead of the Session's persisted View preference (readConversationViewPreference), because the forked File view cannot restore what it was showing — see src/apply.ts's activateLandingView and DefaultConversationViews.tsx's landing effect.

adds: runs the vendor preview engine's own apply(), so every tab type, dictionary, service, seat, chip title and renderer it registers is registered here too — including renderers added in a later release, which nothing here enumerates
redirects exactly one registration: the seat moves from the right Sidebar's sidebar.right.pane.tab to the File tab's conversation.file.document

registers a hand-off body under the vacated Sidebar seat, so openResource (which throws for an unclaimed address) keeps resolving for conversation file links and tool line references, and forwards them to the File tab
one document-host locale namespace holding the hand-off refusal line

re-exports the vendor row's own Host half (apply + Config) from this package's `.` entry, so the `webserver/index-inject` push of __DSH_DOCUMENT_PREVIEW_CONFIG__ — the preview engine's office/excel cache limits — survives the row being disabled instead of falling to schema defaults with no way to set them

the File tab's own View/Edit/Diff/Save controls register into the engine's `sidebar.right.tab.document.actions` toolbar seat (from dsh-plugins-client-ui-conversation-files), so a previewed file carries one row of controls rather than the engine's toolbar under the tab's own header
divergences: A file resource opened through openResource no longer renders in the right Sidebar: the tab claims the address, forwards it to the conversation's File tab, and closes itself. That is the point of the replacement, not a shortfall — but a caller that expected the content to appear in the Sidebar column sees it appear in the middle instead.

The hand-off needs dsh-plugins-client-ui-conversation-files (the File tab) and dsh-plugins-client-ui-conversation-enhanced (the cross-session opener) composed in. Without them the Sidebar tab shows a refusal line instead of a preview, where the vendor row would have previewed the file. Both ship in this same bundle, so the gap only opens if the bundle is taken apart.

The seat reports a settled presentation to its bodies — expanded, never fullscreen, one pane id — because the File tab has no collapsed or fullscreen state to report. A body that varies its behaviour by those flags behaves as though the Sidebar were always open, which in the File tab it effectively is.

Preview settings are configured on this row rather than the vendor's: a profile that set `ui-sidebar-documentpreview`'s office/excel limits sets them on `document-host` now. The schema, its defaults and the injected global are upstream's own, re-exported unchanged, so only the key moves.

adds: threads an optional authorization service through ModelsSection into ProviderEditor
renders AuthorizationPanel beside the API-key field for any row the flow registry claims
four signIn* copy keys in both dictionaries
divergences: apply() does not fall back to the pristine ui-settings-models apply() on setup failure (the other two replacements do) — importing that file for its apply value pulls in its narrower LocaleNamespaceMap declaration, which this package's wider one conflicts with. See src/client/index.ts's own doc comment.

forkOnly.why: Adds a streamable-http-oauth transport to the mcp-client bridge. createTransport is reached through a plain relative import no seam can redirect, so adding a transport case means owning the file that calls it. Disables no vendor row: @deepseek-ai/dsh-mcp-client stays installable and instantiable beside it.

retirements.why: A second file tree, in the other Sidebar. This bundle's own tree predates it, is the one carrying git status and in-app editing, and is where this bundle's users already work. Keeping both means two trees disagreeing about the same directory, so the vendor row is switched off rather than mirrored.
covers: the tree itself, its lazy one-level-at-a-time listing and its open-a-file gesture — dsh-plugins-client-ui-workspace-files' FilesNode, in the left Sidebar
live per-directory watching, the auto-refresh pause/resume toggle and manual reload — ported into FilesNode/useLevel over this bundle's own workspace-scoped workspace-files.watchDirectory stream
per-directory failure lines instead of one generic load error — FilesNode's failureLine
directories-first natural name order — moved Host-side into listWorkspaceEntries' collator
the shared per-extension FileTypeIcon glyphs — FileRow
the workspace.files command (same id, same Cmd+P / Ctrl+Alt+P defaults, same regions), re-registered by dsh-plugins-client-ui-workspace-files' own apply(), now revealing the left-Sidebar tree
divergences: The `files` right-Sidebar tab type is not re-registered anywhere: there is no second tree, which is the point of the retirement. Nothing else registered that kind, so no other package's openTab('files') breaks.
Its Start-page guide tile is gone with the type. The left tree is always present in the Sidebar it lives in, so it needs no entry box to be discovered.

The retired tree was Session-scoped (it listed the Session's workspace root). The left tree is Workspace-scoped, so it also works with a Workspace selected and no Session started — strictly more, but not the same addressing.

The root path is shown on the header row's hover title rather than as a dedicated PathLabel header line: the enclosing Workspace group already names the workspace, so a standalone page's need to state where it is does not apply.
